title: SHADOWBENCH: Toward Reliable Automatic Evaluation of Semantic Alignment in Autoformalization
title_ko: SHADOWBENCH: 자동 형식화에서 의미 정렬의 신뢰할 수 있는 자동 평가를 향하여
abstract: Autoformalization translates informal mathematical theorems into code for proof assistants such as Lean. A central challenge is that current evaluation metrics can accept type-correct but misaligned statements or reject correct statements written in a different formulation. Inspired by Pass@$k$, we propose SA-Pass (*Semantic Alignment Pass*), which tests formal statements using auxiliary statements called *shadows* that characterize the intended statement. A generated statement receives full credit only when it compiles, implies each shadow (forward check), and is implied by their conjunction (backward check). We instantiate SA-Pass in ShadowBench, a Lean 4 full autoformalization benchmark of 178 postgraduate- to research-level problems spanning eight mathematical areas. Claude Code (Opus 4.8) with Numina-Lean-Agent reaches $61.8\%$ compile rate and $11.2\%$ SA-Pass. Across outputs generated by six agentic configurations, SA-Pass achieves $98.8\%$ binary agreement with expert judgments. An early version of ShadowBench served as the benchmark for Track 4 of the ICML 2026 AI4Math Challenge.

definitions:
import Mathlib

set_option autoImplicit false

namespace Arxiv260829270

/-- A finite set of shadow statements `S` is complete if the conjunction of all shadows is logically equivalent to the intended theorem `T`. Formally: `(∀ S ∈ S, T → S) ∧ ((∀ S ∈ S, S) → T)`. -/
def completeShadowSet (T : Prop) (S : Finset Prop) : Prop :=
  (∀ s ∈ S, T → s) ∧ ((∀ s ∈ S, s) → T)

/-- The condition that a generated statement `T_hat` implies every shadow `S` in the set `S`. Formally: `∀ S ∈ S, T_hat → S`. -/
def forwardCheck (T_hat : Prop) (S : Finset Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ s ∈ S, T_hat → s

/-- The condition that the conjunction of all shadows in `S` implies the generated statement `T_hat`. Formally: `(∀ S ∈ S, S) → T_hat`. -/
def backwardCheck (T_hat : Prop) (S : Finset Prop) : Prop :=
  (∀ s ∈ S, s) → T_hat

end Arxiv260829270

items.name: Full autoformalization task
items.tex:
Given an informal theorem statement and its proof, the full autoformalization
task is to generate a formal statement $\widehat T$ together with a
machine-checkable proof of $\widehat T$.
Let $T$ denote the intended formal statement.
The semantic alignment objective is
$\widehat T \Leftrightarrow T$.

items.name: Shadow theorem
items.tex:
For an intended formal statement $T$, a shadow theorem consists of an auxiliary
formal statement $S$ and a machine-checkable proof of $S$.


Its forward checker theorem states that $T$ implies $S$:
\[
T \Rightarrow S.
\]

items.name: Complete shadow set
items.tex:
Let $T$ be the intended formal statement, and let
$\mathcal{S}=\{S_1,\ldots,S_n\}$ be a finite set of shadow statements.
The set $\mathcal{S}$ is \emph{complete} if the shadows jointly characterize
$T$, i.e., the backward checker theorem states
\[
S_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge S_n \Rightarrow T.
\]
Together with the forward checker theorems $T \Rightarrow S_i$, this gives
$S_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge S_n \Leftrightarrow T$.

items.name: Bundled conclusions
items.tex:
Suppose $A,B_1,\ldots,B_n$ are predicates and the intended formal statement has
the form
\[
A \Rightarrow B_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge B_n.
\]
For each $i$, define a shadow theorem
\[
S_i : A \Rightarrow B_i.
\]
Then $\mathcal{S}$ is complete, because the individual components can be
assembled back into the bundled conclusion.

\Cref{app:complete-shadow-bundled,app:complete-shadow-equality} show the corresponding Lean checkers.

items.name: Passing condition
items.tex:
For a problem whose intended formal statement is $T$, a generated formal theorem
with statement $\widehat T$ passes if and only if its declaration and proof type-check
in Lean and it passes the forward checks
\[
\widehat T \Rightarrow S_1,\quad
\widehat T \Rightarrow S_2,\quad \ldots,\quad
\widehat T \Rightarrow S_n
\]
and the backward check
\[
S_1 \wedge \cdots \wedge S_n \Rightarrow \widehat T,
\]
where $\mathcal{S}=\{S_1,\ldots,S_n\}$ is a complete shadow set for $T$.

items.name: \ourmetric
\ourrelaxed
items.tex:
Let $\widehat T$ be the statement of a generated formal theorem, and let
$\mathcal{S}=\{S_1,\ldots,S_n\}$ be a complete shadow set.
If the generated theorem does not type-check in Lean, set
$\text{\ourrelaxed}(\widehat T,\mathcal{S}){=}0$.



Otherwise, its \ourrelaxed score is
\begin{multline}
\text{\ourrelaxed}(\widehat T,\mathcal{S}) := 
\frac{1}{2}\cdot
\underbracket[0.5pt][2pt]{
\frac{|\{i : \widehat T \Rightarrow S_i\}|}{|\mathcal{S}|}}_{\text{forward checks}} \\
+
\frac{1}{2}\cdot
\underbracket[0.5pt][2pt]{
\mathbf{1}\{\bigwedge_{i=1}^n S_i \Rightarrow \widehat T\}}_{\text{backward check}}. \nonumber
\end{multline}
Here $\mathbf{1}\{\phi\}$ equals $1$ if the corresponding checker theorem
type-checks in Lean, and $0$ otherwise.

If a generated statement $\widehat T$ passes the SA-Pass metric (i.e., $\text{SA-Pass}(\widehat T, \mathcal{S}) = 1$) with respect to a complete shadow set $\mathcal{S}$ for the intended theorem $T$, then $\widehat T$ is logically equivalent to $T$ ($\widehat T \Leftrightarrow T$).

(Basis: Definition 4 states that passing requires forward checks ($\widehat T \Rightarrow S_i$ for all $i$) and a backward check ($\bigwedge S_i \Rightarrow \widehat T$). Definition 3 states that for a complete shadow set, $\bigwedge S_i \Leftrightarrow T$. Combining these: $\widehat T \Rightarrow S_i$ implies $\widehat T \Rightarrow \bigwedge S_i$, and since $\bigwedge S_i \Leftrightarrow T$, we have $\widehat T \Rightarrow T$. Conversely, $\bigwedge S_i \Rightarrow \widehat T$ and $T \Rightarrow \bigwedge S_i$ (from completeness) imply $T \Rightarrow \widehat T$. Thus $\widehat T \Leftrightarrow T$.)

Combining these: $\widehat T \Rightarrow S_i$ implies $\widehat T \Rightarrow \bigwedge S_i$, and since $\bigwedge S_i \Leftrightarrow T$, we have $\widehat T \Rightarrow T$. Conversely, $\bigwedge S_i \Rightarrow \widehat T$ and $T \Rightarrow \bigwedge S_i$ (from completeness) imply $T \Rightarrow \widehat T$. Thus $\widehat T \Leftrightarrow T$.

items.tex:
If a generated statement $\widehat T$ is logically equivalent to the intended theorem $T$ ($\widehat T \Leftrightarrow T$) and $\mathcal{S}$ is a complete shadow set for $T$, then $\widehat T$ passes the SA-Pass metric (assuming $\widehat T$ compiles).

(Basis: Definition 3 defines completeness as $T \Rightarrow S_i$ and $\bigwedge S_i \Rightarrow T$. If $\widehat T \Leftrightarrow T$, then $\widehat T \Rightarrow T \Rightarrow S_i$ (forward check holds) and $\bigwedge S_i \Rightarrow T \Leftrightarrow \widehat T$ (backward check holds). Definition 4 states that passing is defined by these checks plus compilation.)

Definition 4 states that passing is defined by these checks plus compilation.
items.statement_en: Let $T$ be the intended theorem, $\widehat{T}$ be a generated statement, and $\mathcal{S}$ be a set of shadow statements. If $\widehat{T}$ is logically equivalent to $T$ (i.e., $\widehat{T} \leftrightarrow T$) and $\mathcal{S}$ is a complete shadow set for $T$, then $\widehat{T}$ passes the SA-Pass metric. Specifically, the forward check holds ($\forall S \in \mathcal{S}, \widehat{T} \to S$) and the backward check holds ($(\forall S \in \mathcal{S}, S) \to \widehat{T}$).
items.statement_ko: $T$를 의도된 정리, $\widehat{T}$를 생성된 명제, $\mathcal{S}$를 그림자 명제들의 집합이라고 하자. 만약 $\widehat{T}$가 $T$와 논리적으로 동치라면 (즉, $\widehat{T} \leftrightarrow T$) 그리고 $\mathcal{S}$가 $T$에 대한 완전한 그림자 집합이라면, $\widehat{T}$는 SA-Pass 지표를 통과한다. 구체적으로, 전방 검사($\forall S \in \mathcal{S}, \widehat{T} \to S$)와 후방 검사($(\forall S \in \mathcal{S}, S) \to \widehat{T}$)가 모두 성립한다.
items.lean: (T T_hat : Prop) (S : Finset Prop) (h_equiv : T_hat ↔ T) (h_complete : completeShadowSet T S) : forwardCheck T_hat S ∧ backwardCheck T_hat S
items.note: The paper defines SA-Pass as the conjunction of forwardCheck, backwardCheck, and compilation. Since compilation is a syntactic property not formalized in the shared definitions, the theorem states the logical core: that equivalence and completeness imply both the forward and backward checks.

items.tex:
Let $\mathcal{S}_1$ and $\mathcal{S}_2$ be two shadow sets such that $\mathcal{S}_1 \subseteq \mathcal{S}_2$. If a generated statement $\widehat T$ passes the forward checks for $\mathcal{S}_2$ (i.e., $\forall s \in \mathcal{S}_2, \widehat T \Rightarrow s$), then it also passes the forward checks for $\mathcal{S}_1$.

(Basis: Definition of `forwardCheck` in Lean: `∀ s ∈ S, T_hat → s`. This is a universal quantification over the set. If the property holds for all elements in a superset, it necessarily holds for all elements in a subset. This is a basic logical property of universal quantification over sets.)

items.tex:
For a generated statement $\widehat T$ that compiles, $\text{SA-Pass}(\widehat T, \mathcal{S}) = 1$ if and only if $\text{Relaxed}(\widehat T, \mathcal{S}) = 1$.

(Basis: Definition 5 defines SA-Pass as 1 iff all forward checks pass AND the backward check passes. Definition 6 defines Relaxed score as $0.5 \times (\text{fraction of forward checks passed}) + 0.5 \times (\text{backward check passed})$. The maximum value of the fraction is 1 (all forward checks pass) and the indicator is 1 (backward check passes). Thus, the sum is 1 iff both components are maximal, which corresponds exactly to the condition for SA-Pass = 1.)

items.tex:
The empty set $\emptyset$ is a complete shadow set for the intended theorem $T$ if and only if $T$ is logically true ($T \Leftrightarrow \top$).

(Basis: Definition 3 (and Lean `completeShadowSet`) defines completeness as $(\forall s \in S, T \to s) \land ((\forall s \in S, s) \to T)$. For $S = \emptyset$, the first conjunct $\forall s \in \emptyset, T \to s$ is vacuously true. The second conjunct $(\forall s \in \emptyset, s) \to T$ simplifies to $\top \to T$, which is equivalent to $T$. Thus, completeness holds iff $T$ is true.)

The second conjunct $(\forall s \in \emptyset, s) \to T$ simplifies to $\top \to T$, which is equivalent to $T$. Thus, completeness holds iff $T$ is true.

items.note: The definition `completeShadowSet` uses `Finset Prop`. The empty set is represented as `∅`. The equivalence holds because the forward direction `∀ s ∈ ∅, T → s` is vacuously true, and the backward direction `(∀ s ∈ ∅, s) → T` simplifies to `True → T`, which is equivalent to `T`.

items.tex:
If a shadow statement $S$ is logically true ($S \Leftrightarrow \top$), then any generated statement $\widehat T$ passes the forward check for $S$ (i.e., $\widehat T \Rightarrow S$ holds).

(Basis: Definition of `forwardCheck` requires $\widehat T \Rightarrow S$. In classical logic, any proposition implies a tautology ($\top$). Therefore, if $S$ is a tautology, the implication holds regardless of $\widehat T$.)
